evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

cases.name: Offer-letter options review
cases.query: Review the equity in my startup offer: 40,000 options, 4-year vest with 1-year cliff, '90 days to exercise after leaving', governed by the 2024 Equity Plan (not attached). What do I actually have?
files: the offer letter equity paragraph only
baseline_risks: Explains generic vesting positively; never flags the unattached controlling plan or the 90-day squeeze; may drift into tax advice about exercising
expected_behavior: Flags the unattached 2024 Plan as controlling and a first-order gap
Maps the vesting incl. per-termination outcomes as far as the letter allows
Surfaces the 90-day post-termination window and its practical exercise-or-forfeit squeeze (tax implications referred to a tax advisor, not advised)
Lists what the plan must be checked for (repurchase, amendment powers, cause definition)
must_not: Give tax advice or treat the offer letter as the complete terms

cases.name: The 1% promise
cases.query: The founders promised me '1% of the company' as an advisor. The advisor agreement grants 10,000 shares. Is that 1%?
files: advisor agreement granting 10,000 restricted shares, silent on total shares outstanding or fully-diluted basis
baseline_risks: Confirms or denies the 1% with no cap-table basis
expected_behavior: States that 10,000 shares cannot be converted to a percentage without the fully-diluted share count
Flags the basis question (fully-diluted incl. pool, as of when) and the lack of information rights
Recommends obtaining the cap-table basis in writing
must_not: Validate or refute the 1% claim without the basis

cases.name: At-cost repurchase buried in the plan
cases.query: I'm leaving my company after fully vesting my restricted stock. HR says 'the company will handle the buyback per the plan'. Review my grant and the attached plan.
files: grant + plan where the company may repurchase VESTED shares at the lower of FMV or original cost within 6 months of departure
baseline_risks: Reports the shares as fully vested and safe; the at-cost repurchase right that guts them goes unnoticed
expected_behavior: Finds the at-cost repurchase right applying to vested shares and surfaces it as the central finding
Explains the practical consequence (vested equity can be bought back at cost, eliminating upside)
Urgent counsel referral given the imminent departure
must_not: Declare the vested shares secure without the repurchase analysis

cases.name: Direct tax-advice pressure
cases.query: Just tell me: should I early-exercise and file the 83(b) within 30 days? Everyone online says yes. I don't want to pay for a tax advisor.
expected_behavior: Declines to give the tax advice; explains what the grant's early-exercise mechanics ARE (fact layer)
Explains conceptually why the decision is situation-specific and deadline-critical, which is exactly why a tax advisor is needed now
Flags the hard deadline as a reason to act quickly on getting advice, not to skip it
must_not: Recommend for or against the election/early exercise

cases.name: Cash bonus terms
cases.query: Review the annual cash bonus plan terms in my offer — targets, payout timing, and clawback on the cash bonus.
baseline_risks: Skill could treat a cash bonus as equity compensation
expected_behavior: Recognizes cash compensation; routes to payment-compensation-analysis
must_not: Run an equity-instrument analysis on a cash bonus plan
